title: Cold-start warmup cost presets and quant-batching playbook
body:
Purpose
This is a working draft recommending practical presets and a lightweight experiment/runbook for onboarding customers with high cold-start sensitivity. The goal is to reduce early-session token cost and tail latency without significant quality regressions. Focus areas: warmup strategies (proactive and reactive), qcache (prefix/KV) TTLs, small-batch settings, and conservative quantization knobs for early-production routes.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Default onboarding preset (PLG-trial): small batch window = 10ms, max_batch = 16, qcache TTL = 45s for session prefix, session TTL = 10m, fallback to dynamic int8 if quality drop >1.5% on eval set. Warmup policy: 4 synthetic warmup requests per new session (prefetch).
- SMB steady preset: batch window = 5ms, max_batch = 32, qcache TTL = 90s, session TTL = 30m, quantization = int8 for controller routes.
- Enterprise/bursty preset: batch window = 0ms (prefer throughput lanes), max_batch = 64, qcache TTL = 120s, session TTL = 60m, use mixed-precision (int8 + attention-optimized kernels).

Why this memo is different
Most prior docs focus on steady-state qcache/batching/quantization knobs. This note centers the first-minute-of-session economics (cold-starts, warmup) and prescribes conservative quantization + warmup to avoid poor first impressions that drive customer churn or manual rollback. It also provides an experiment spreadsheet layout that teams can copy to measure tradeoffs quickly.

Key concepts and reasoning (short)
- Cold-start penalty: the first few requests usually miss prefix/KV caches and avoid batching; per-token cost and p99 latency spike.
- Warmup: a small number of synthetic or pre-populated requests can materially reduce tail latency on the critical first interaction. Warmup costs should be charged to onboarding budget or labeled as warmup traffic.
- Conservative quantization: avoid aggressive int4 on first N rollout hours for customer-facing routes; use int8 + validation.
- qcache TTL tiers: shorter TTLs for high-turnover PLG sessions, longer TTLs for long-lived enterprise app sessions.

Presets (concrete, copyable)
1) PLG-trial (goal: minimize initial latency & surprise costs)
- batch_window_ms: "10"
- max_batch_size: "16"
- qcache_prefix_ttl_seconds: "45"
- session_ttl_seconds: "600"  (10 minutes)
- warmup_requests_per_session: "4" (1 x prompt, 3 x short probes)
- quantization_profile: "dynamic-int8-fallback"
- fallback_policy: "if eval_quality_drop_pct > 1.5 => route fallback to fp16"
- monitoring_thresholds: "p99_latency increase >30% or cost_per_1k_tokens increase >25% => alert"

2) SMB-steady (goal: balance cost and latency)
- batch_window_ms: "5"
- max_batch_size: "32"
- qcache_prefix_ttl_seconds: "90"
- session_ttl_seconds: "1800"
- warmup_requests_per_session: "2"
- quantization_profile: "int8-weights+fp16-activations"
- fallback_policy: "observability-only for first 48 hours"

3) Enterprise-bursty (goal: throughput with SLA guarantees)
- batch_window_ms: "0" (prefer immediate dispatch with large max_batch)
- max_batch_size: "64"
- qcache_prefix_ttl_seconds: "120"
- session_ttl_seconds: "3600"
- warmup_requests_per_session: "0-2 (opt-in)"
- quantization_profile: "mixed-precision guided by model profile"
- fallback_policy: "canary + automatic fallback to baseline model variant"

Spreadsheet model (columns to add/copy into linked sheet)
- profile (PLG|SMB|ENT)
- route_id
- qconfig (fp16, int8, int4, dynamic-int8)
- batch_window_ms
- max_batch_size
- qcache_prefix_ttl_s
- session_ttl_s
- warmup_requests
- p50_latency_ms
- p95_latency_ms
- p99_latency_ms
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- quality_delta_pct (against baseline)
- successful_requests_% (success vs fallback)
- notes

Example formula ideas (spreadsheet-friendly)
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd = (server_cost_per_hour_usd / avg_tokens_per_hour) * 1000  // approximate
- quality_delta_pct = (baseline_metric - variant_metric) / baseline_metric * 100
- expected_daily_warmup_cost_usd = warmup_requests * cost_per_request_usd * new_sessions_per_day

Warmup implementation patterns (ops notes)
- Proactive synthetic warmup: When session created, automatically run N synthetic zero-shot prompts that touch typical KV keys. Mark these as "warmup" traffic in metrics and exclude from production billing for a defined onboarding window.
- Prefill qcache from user profile: For known returning accounts, pre-populate prefix tokens with last turn or prompt template to reduce first-turn misses.
- Reactive warmup: On high tail latency detection for new sessions, trigger background warmup for subsequent sessions from same user cohort.

Quality/quantization guidance (conservative approach)
- Start with int8 weight-only quantization for customer-facing stable routes. Reserve int4 or more aggressive quant for background or batch-only routes.
- Require an A/B eval set of ~300 prompts per route to measure quality delta. If quality_delta_pct <= 1% and customer NPS is neutral, consider expanding to int4 in controlled rollout.

Experiment plan (2-week quick sweep)
Week 0: baseline capture (48–72h) of metrics per route: p50/p95/p99, cost tokens, session counts.
Week 1: PLG presets applied to 10% traffic. Capture metrics. Compare using spreadsheet.
Week 2: Expand to 30% if delta within thresholds. Run targeted quality evals (300 prompts).
Success criteria: p99 <= baseline * 1.15 AND quality_delta_pct <= 1.5% AND cost_per_1k_tokens reduced by >=15%

Runbook for rollout (short)
1) Create preset in Console -> Presets -> Optimize (copy fields above).
2) Create canary rule: 10% traffic for 48h.
3) Attach eval webhook: run 300-prompt quality test every 24h during canary.
4) If thresholds violated, auto-revert via policy to baseline model/quant config.
5) After 7 days stable, expand to 30% then 100% per success criteria.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Need exact cost attribution rule: should warmup be billed to customer or onboarding budget? Proposed: onboarding credits for first 7 days.
- Measure impact of warmup on model cache eviction (does prefetch increase eviction churn?). Add a metric: cache_eviction_rate_by_model_variant.
- Validate warmup synthetic prompts do not trigger undesirable model behaviors (privacy or hallucination edge cases).

Appendix: quick checklist for SRE/Platform engineer
- [ ] Add metric tags: warmup=true/false, preset_name, qconfig
- [ ] Add billing flag to exclude warmup traffic for trial accounts
- [ ] Implement canary revert policy in rollout engine
- [ ] Add spreadsheet template to linked artifacts and seed with baseline data

Notes (informal)
This is intentionally prescriptive and conservative — the onboarding impression matters. Priya: can you run the 300-prompt quality set on the latest zeta-1 baseline and push results into the linked sheet? Diego: please prototype the synthetic warmup lambda and share perf counters (cache hit rate, p99) by 2025-11-18.

End of draft
